'''Oskar Johann Viktor Anderson''' ({{langx|ru|Оскар Николаевич Андерсон|translit=Oskar Nikolayevich Anderson}}; {{Gregorian to Julian|2 August 1887}} – 12 February 1960) was a Russian-German [[mathematician]] of [[Baltic Germans|Baltic German]] descent. He is best known for his work on [[mathematical statistics]] and [[econometrics]].

== Life ==
Anderson was born into [[Baltic German]] family in [[Minsk]] in the [[Russian Empire]] (present-day Belarus), but soon moved to [[Kazan]]. His father, [[Nikolai Anderson]], was professor in [[Finno-Ugric languages]] at the [[University of Kazan]].<ref name="srkNik">{{citation |author= <!--unknown administrators--> |language= ru |title= Формулярный списокь (service record): Николай Андерсон (Nikolai Anderson) |url= http://www.earchive-estlatrus.eu/web/guest/collections?p_p_id=earchivecatalog_WAR_earchiveportlet&p_p_lifecycle=0&p_p_state=normal&p_p_mode=view&p_p_col_id=column-1&p_p_col_pos=1&p_p_col_count=2&p_r_p_-714710835_view=document&_earchivecatalog_WAR_earchiveportlet_documentId=14697 |work= Oskar Nikolaevich Anderson (1907-1912) |publisher= Archives of the [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University|Petrograd Polytechnical Institute of the Emperor Peter the Great]] in the Central State Historical Archives of St. Petersburg |location= St. Petersburg |pages= 9–18 |access-date= 2018-10-27 |archive-date= 2016-03-05 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160305064715/http://www.earchive-estlatrus.eu/web/guest/collections?p_p_id=earchivecatalog_WAR_earchiveportlet&p_p_lifecycle=0&p_p_state=normal&p_p_mode=view&p_p_col_id=column-1&p_p_col_pos=1&p_p_col_count=2&p_r_p_-714710835_view=document&_earchivecatalog_WAR_earchiveportlet_documentId=14697 |url-status= dead }}</ref> His older brothers were the [[folklorist]] [[Walter Anderson (folklorist)|Walter Anderson]] and the [[astrophysicist]] [[Wilhelm Anderson]].<ref name="rafikova">{{Cite journal|last1 = Рафикова (Rafikova)|first1 = Г. (G.)|last2 = Ибрагимова (Ibrahimova)|first2 = Ф. (F.)| title = Биографика Казанского университета: Андерсоны (Kazan University Biography: Anderson)|language= ru| url=http://echovek.ru/ru/article/g-rafikova-f-ibragimova-biografika-kazanskogo-universitetaandersony |url-access=subscription | journal = Гасырлар авазы – Эхо веков | volume = 2016 1/2 | year=2016 }}</ref>

Oskar Anderson graduated from [[Kazan Gymnasium]] with a gold medal in 1906. After studying [[mathematics]] for one year at [[Kazan Federal University]], he moved to [[St. Petersburg]] to study [[economics]] at [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University]].<ref name="srk1">{{citation |author= <!--unknown administrators--> |language= ru |title= Оскар Николаевич Андерсон (1907-1912) / Oskar Nikolaevich Anderson (1907-1912) |url= http://www.earchive-estlatrus.eu/web/guest/collections?p_p_id=earchivecatalog_WAR_earchiveportlet&p_p_lifecycle=0&p_p_state=normal&p_p_mode=view&p_p_col_id=column-1&p_p_col_pos=1&p_p_col_count=2&p_r_p_-714710835_view=document&_earchivecatalog_WAR_earchiveportlet_documentId=14697 |id= TsGIASpb 478 1 64 |publisher= Archives of the [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University|Petrograd Polytechnical Institute of the Emperor Peter the Great]] in the Central State Historical Archives of St. Petersburg |location= St. Petersburg |access-date= 2018-10-27 |archive-date= 2016-03-05 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160305064715/http://www.earchive-estlatrus.eu/web/guest/collections?p_p_id=earchivecatalog_WAR_earchiveportlet&p_p_lifecycle=0&p_p_state=normal&p_p_mode=view&p_p_col_id=column-1&p_p_col_pos=1&p_p_col_count=2&p_r_p_-714710835_view=document&_earchivecatalog_WAR_earchiveportlet_documentId=14697 |url-status= dead }}</ref><ref name="srk2">{{citation |author=<!--unknown administrators--> |language= ru |title= Андерсон Оскар Николаевич - стипендиат (1912-1914) / Oskar Nikolaevich Anderson - scholarship holder (1912-1914) |url=http://www.earchive-estlatrus.eu/web/guest/collections?p_p_id=earchivecatalog_WAR_earchiveportlet&p_p_lifecycle=0&p_p_state=normal&p_p_mode=view&p_p_col_id=column-1&p_p_col_pos=1&p_p_col_count=2&p_r_p_-714710835_view=document&_earchivecatalog_WAR_earchiveportlet_documentId=14659 |id= TsGIASpb 478 23 5|publisher = Archives of the [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University|Petrograd Polytechnical Institute of the Emperor Peter the Great]] in the Central State Historical Archives of St. Petersburg |location = St. Petersburg|access-date= 2018-10-27 }}</ref> From 1907 to 1915, he was [[Alexander Alexandrovich Chuprov|Aleksandr Chuprov]]'s student and assistant. In 1912, he married Margarethe Natalie von Hindenburg-Hirtenberg,<ref name="statprob" /> a granddaughter of {{ill|Wilhelm Paul von Hindenburg-Hirtenberg|ru|Гинденбург, Василий Данилович|}},<ref>{{cite encyclopedia | last1 = Снапкоўскі
  | first1 = Юрый | encyclopedia = Гербоўнік беларускай шляхты | title = ГІНДЭНБУРГІ, ПАСТОРЫУСЫ дэ ГІНДЭНБУРГІ (HINDENBURG, PASTORYUS de HINDENBURG) герба "БРОХВІЧ I" | language = be | pages = 372–379 | volume = 4 | year = 2016 }}</ref> who was commemorated in "The Funeral of 'The Universal Man'" in [[Fyodor Dostoyevsky]]'s ''[[A Writer's Diary]]'', and started lecturing at a commercial school in St. Petersburg while also studying for a law degree at [[Saint Petersburg State University]], graduating in 1914.<ref name="statprob">{{cite encyclopedia
  | last1 = Strecker 
  | first1 = Heinrich
  | last2 = Strecker
  | first2 = Rosemarie
  | encyclopedia = Encyclopedia of Mathematics
  | title = Oskar Anderson
  | url = http://www.encyclopediaofmath.org/index.php?title=Anderson,_Oskar&oldid=39172
  | publisher = Springer-Verlag GmbH, Heidelberg
  | year = 2016
 }}</ref>

In 1918, he took on a professorship in [[Kiev]] but he was forced to flee Russia in 1920 due to the [[Russian Revolution]], first taking a post in [[Budapest]], Hungary, before becoming a professor at the [[University of Economics Varna]] in [[Bulgaria]], in 1924.
 
Anderson was one of the charter members of the [[Econometric Society]],<ref name="fels">{{cite journal| last = Fels | first = Eberhard | date = 1961 | title = Oskar Anderson, 1887-1960 | journal = [[Econometrica]] | volume = 29 | issue = 1 | pages = 74–79 | doi = 10.2307/1907689  | jstor = 1907689| jstor-access = free }}</ref> whose members also elected him to be a fellow of the society in 1933.<ref>{{cite web | title=In Memoriam | work=List of Deceased Fellows of the Econometric Society | url=https://www.econometricsociety.org/society/organization-and-governance/fellows/memoriam | access-date=April 4, 2019 }}</ref><ref name="fels" /> In the same year, he also received a fellowship from the [[Rockefeller Foundation]].<ref name="faure">{{citation | last = Faure | first = Justine | title = The Rockefeller Foundation Fellows in Social Sciences: Transnational Networks and Construction of Disciplines — The Example of East Central Europe | url = https://rockarch.issuelab.org/resource/the-rockefeller-foundation-fellows-in-social-sciences-transnational-networks-and-construction-of-disciplines-the-example-of-east-central-europe.html|publisher = [[Rockefeller Archive Center]] | year = 2012}}</ref>

Supported by the foundation, in 1935 he established and became director of the Statistical Institute for Economic Research at [[Sofia University]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Avramov |first=Roumen |editor-last=Kovács |editor-first=János Mátyás |title=Populating No Man's Land: Economic Concepts of Ownership under Communism |publisher=Rowman & Littlefield |date=September 2018 |pages=23–46 |chapter=Chapter 1: From Nationalization to Nowhere. Ownership in Bulgarian Economic Thought (1944–1989) |isbn=978-1-4985-3921-0}}</ref> For the remainder of the decade, he also served the [[League of Nations]] as an associate member of its Committee of Statistical Experts.<ref>{{cite report | author = <!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> | year = 1938 | title = The Rockefeller Foundation Annual Report 1937 | chapter-url = https://assets.rockefellerfoundation.org/app/uploads/20150530122132/Annual-Report-1937.pdf | publisher = [[Rockefeller Foundation|The Rockefeller Foundation]] | chapter = Report of Work in the Social Sciences | page = 258 | access-date = 2018-11-07 }}</ref>

In 1942, he joined the [[Kiel Institute for the World Economy]] as the head of the Department of Eastern Studies and also took up a full professorship of statistics at [[Kiel University]],<ref name="statprob"/> where he was joined by his brother Walter after the end of the [[Second World War]]. In 1947, he took a position at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]], teaching there until 1956, when he retired.

== Writings ==
* ''Einführung in die Mathematische Statistik'', [[Vienna]]: [[Springer Verlag|Springer-Verlag]], 1935, {{ISBN|978-3-7091-5873-9}} <ref>{{cite book | last = Anderson | first = Oskar N. | title = Einführung in die Mathematische Statistik | publisher = Springer-Verlag Wien | date = 1935 | language = de | doi = 10.1007/978-3-7091-5923-1 | zbl = 0012.11104 }}</ref>
* ''Über die repräsentative Methode und deren Anwendung auf die Aufarbeitung der Ergebnisse der bulgarischen landwirtschaftlichen Betriebszählung vom 31. Dezember 1926'', Munich: {{ill|Bayerisches Landesamt für Statistik|lt=Bayer. Statist. Landesamt|de|Bayerisches Landesamt für Statistik}}, 1949
* ''Die Saisonschwankungen in der deutschen Stromproduktion vor und nach dem Kriege'', Munich: [[Ifo Institute for Economic Research|Inst. f. Wirtschaftsforschung]], 1950
